written.text: Write a precis of the following passage by reducing it to one third of its length(10) Reading is one of the most valuable habits a person can develop. It opens up new worlds, ideas, and perspectives, enriching the mind and imagination. Through books, articles, and other written materials, people gain knowledge about history, science, culture, and human behaviour. Reading also improves language skills, vocabulary, and critical thinking. It encourages curiosity and creativity, allowing individuals to explore concepts beyond their immediate experiences. Furthermore, reading can be a source of relaxation and stress relief, offering an escape from the pressures of daily life. In a world full of distractions, dedicating time to read helps cultivate discipline and focus. Societies that encourage reading tend to be more informed, empathetic, and innovative. Thus, reading is not merely a pastime but a lifelong tool for personal growth and societal advancement.

You are Mr. XYZ living in MINECO. Write a letter of complaint to the Mayor, Aizawl Municipal Corporation regarding the lack of sufficient street lights in your area which has drawn antisocial elements and has increased criminal activities in your neighbourhood.(10)

Read the following passage and answer the questions based on the given passage. Studies serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability. Their chief use for delight is in privateness and retiring; for ornament is in this course; and for ability is in the judgment and disposition of business. For expert men can execute, and perhaps judge of particulars, one by one; but the general counsels, and the plots and marshalling of affairs, come best, from those that are learned. To spend too much time in studies is sloth; to use them too much for ornaments is affectation; to make judgement wholly by their rules, is the humour of a scholar. They perfect nature, and are perfected by experience: for natural abilities are like natural plants that need pruning, by study; and studies themselves do give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded in by experience. Crafty men condemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by observation. Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse but to weigh and consider.
